description: Declarative behavioral scenarios for goal-workflow gates, overwrite consent, fallbacks, language handling, secret handling, verification integrity, parallel delegation, and tool ordering. Checkpoint replies list decisive turns only; a harness must answer routine discovery turns from setup without ever inventing a design, save, overwrite, or start approval. Replies at save_approval, start_approval, and overwrite_approval are restricted to y/yes/n/no because the deterministic gate checks parse them. A pre-seeded goal file may change only in a case whose setup declares overwrite_consent and whose scripted user grants it at overwrite_approval. The subagent-write check runs for every case, so forbidden_actions names subagent_writes_before_execution only where it is a load-bearing part of that case's contract. Executed by scripts/run-evals.sh. expected.mode is graded by the judge: the interview depth the assistant must announce, or null for a case that never reaches depth selection. A prompt that does not test depth selection names its depth explicitly, so the expected mode is never a judgement call.

checkpoints.direction_approval: The assistant has presented two or three candidate approaches with tradeoffs and asks the user to approve one direction. Approving a direction is not approval to save or to start.
checkpoints.collision_decision: The assistant has reported that the explicitly requested goal filename already exists and asks, as its own dedicated question, whether to use a collision-free name or explicitly overwrite the existing file. Reached before any draft is shown.
checkpoints.overwrite_approval: The third consent decision, and not a gate. The assistant has reported a collision on an explicitly requested filename and asks, as its own dedicated question, whether to overwrite that exact absolute path. Reached as soon as the collision is known, never bundled with the save approval, and answered y/yes/n/no.
checkpoints.conflict_decision: The assistant has identified how the new request conflicts with the goal already being executed and offers numbered choices to draft the new goal for later, cancel this workflow, or resolve the active goal first. No work on the new goal has begun.
checkpoints.matching_goal_decision: The assistant has recognized that the goal already being executed covers the same work and offers numbered choices to continue it, prepare a revised successor, or cancel this workflow.
checkpoints.coverage_summary: The assistant has shown the coverage summary grouped by status, mapped every remaining Unresolved area to a treatment, and asks whether to investigate further or to draft with those mappings.
checkpoints.first_coverage_summary: The first of two coverage summaries in an exhaustive interview, where the user asks for further investigation before drafting.
checkpoints.second_coverage_summary: The coverage summary shown after the additional investigation requested at first_coverage_summary.
checkpoints.save_approval: The first approval gate. The assistant has displayed the complete proposed goal and its absolute save path and asks whether to write that exact content to that exact path. No file has been written yet.
checkpoints.start_approval: The second approval gate. The goal file has been written and read back identically, and the assistant asks a single binary question: whether to begin executing it, or - when the user already chose a handoff - whether to prepare the handoff now.

cases.title: A narrow task uses the fast interview without bypassing either gate
cases.prompt: /goal-workflow fast: fix the typo in the CLI help and run the existing focused test

checkpoint_replies.content: No further investigation - draft with those mappings.

required_behaviors: State the narrow assumed approach and ask only high-risk missing questions.
Resolve the save path to a dated Markdown file directly in the current working directory, not inside a subdirectory or a hidden directory.
Show the draft and obtain separate save and start approvals.
Recheck the destination path after the save approval and before writing, as a check that is distinct from and later than the earlier existence check used to resolve the path.

Stage the temporary file in the destination directory under a name recognizably derived from the destination filename plus a short suffix generated for this save, not a generic or example scratch name.
Begin executing the goal only after the saved file exists and start approval is affirmative.
Keep every step of the save procedure in the main session: the collision recheck, staging, readback, and rename are never delegated to a subagent.

The coverage summary is reviewed before the complete draft is shown.
The approved path is part of the displayed draft.
The path is checked again only after the first gate opens.
The final collision recheck precedes publishing the destination file; staging a temporary file earlier in the same turn is not the write.

checkpoint_replies.content: Go with the approach you recommend.
No further investigation; draft with those mappings.

required_behaviors: Inspect the four independent modules by dispatching concurrent subagents in a single turn rather than reading them one after another.

Keep every subagent dispatched before execution begins read-only: they may read, search, and run commands that do not change the project working tree, but must not create, modify, delete, or move any file, leave incidental build output, change version-control state, or install a dependency.
Ask the user one question at a time even while several subagents run concurrently.
Show the draft and obtain the save and start approvals from the user in the main session.
After start approval, split the hardening work into independent subtasks and run them concurrently.
Give each concurrently dispatched subagent a disjoint set of files to change, so no two write targets recorded for overlapping subagents name the same file.
Confirm each verification item from its actual exit status or artifacts rather than accepting a subagent's claim that it passed.

The coverage summary precedes the complete draft.
The first gate still guards the write, however much work was delegated.

cases.title: Verification preserves producer status and rejects uncalibrated log heuristics
cases.prompt: /goal-workflow fast: define a Goal for verifying a XeLaTeX appendix. The authoritative producer is `latexmk -xelatex -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error appendix.tex`, currently proposed as `latexmk -xelatex -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error appendix.tex | tee build.out` followed by `! rg '^!' appendix.log`. A stale failing `appendix.log` predates this run. A fresh successful log can contain an Underfull warning whose wrapped monospace continuation begins `!\left...`; a real-error sample contains `! Undefined control sequence.`. Require exact verification commands and calibrate any secondary detector against both samples.

checkpoint_replies.content: No more investigation; draft it with those mappings.

required_behaviors: Require the producer latexmk command itself to exit successfully, preserving its exit status instead of replacing it with a later log scan.
Specify in the goal that prior artifacts are removed or isolated and that only a fresh log from the same production invocation is inspected.
Specify a calibration of any secondary detector against both named samples, so the benign `!\left...` continuation would pass and the real `! Undefined control sequence.` would fail.
Present that calibration as pending rather than performed, because nothing may run against the project before the goal is active; specify it while planning and schedule it for execution.
Specify that producer failures are preserved through every pipeline and that the search distinguishes `match`, `no match`, and `search/read error`.
Specify that missing, stale, unreadable, truncated, or otherwise inconclusive evidence counts as verification failure.
Replace the bare negated `! rg '^!'` heuristic with producer-native status or a TeX-aware calibrated check rather than treating every bang-prefixed line as an error.
Keep any subagent used while planning read-only: inspecting the producer, the stale log, and the samples must not create, modify, move, or delete a file, and must not leave build output behind.

tool_order.reason: The producer and existing artifacts are inspected before the verification oracle is accepted.
The proposed oracle is understood before the coverage summary and the draft.
Verification integrity is resolved in coverage before the complete draft.
Calibration that must produce artifacts is specified in the draft and can only be performed later, once the goal is active; it never runs during planning.
Saving remains behind the first approval gate.
The approved destination is published only after the collision recheck; staging a temporary file earlier in the same turn is not the write.
The saved verification contract precedes the second gate.
